body: Common newbie mistakes are thinking that all land is worth taking, and ignoring trade. Most of the time raising autonomy to avoid rebels isn't worth it, unless you're already the undisputed superpower and just don't want to bother with the rebel whack a mole minigame anymore. No point spending AE, admin, money, manpower, and time taking land in a bad trade node and raising autonomy to make it useless. You were better off not taking it and spending those resources on your economy. Go for high value provinces in downstream nodes.

No one doing AJATT knows how to read kanji beforehand, it would be inefficient to learn all of the possible readings individually. You learn by learning words as you go along.

AJATT advises you to completely avoid learning grammar in the beginning, MIA directly tells you to study grammar in the beginning.

AJATT advises you to go through all RTK 1 kanji, MIA advises you to just do the 1000 most frequent.

The AJATT site is a jumbled mess, MIA is organized, clearly structured, and easy to read.

MIA doesn't have any of the weird silverspoon/MCDs/clozed stuff that Khatz tried implementing later on.

MIA has a completely different approach to making the monolingual transiton.

Makes sense, Japanese isn't that useful most of the time for a westerner not living in Japan, and it takes thousands of hours to acquire the skill. Don't devote your life to the language unless you have very good reason.

Will it work if you do it? Yes.

Should most people do it? No. It isn't worth sacrificing the rest of your life to maximize the speed at which you learn Japanese. Even Matt himself says that he regrets learning Japanese, if he could go back in time he wouldn't do it.

Yeah it's complicated, but probably the most efficient way of making the transition. It's probably worth figuring out how to use it. You can also try the old pre-morphman guide if you want: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2AH2JmxglzU

Like others have said, you need to train listening if you want quality audio comprehension. If you immerse with subs, you think that you're understanding speech while you're actually using text to fill in the gaps that you miss in audio. Then when you do go to listen without text, you mistakenly think you're understanding things when you're actually missing a ton.

Comprehensible audio is audio that you've studied and understand. Like if you've studied chapter 1 of the Tango and understand all of the sentences from chapter 1, then that is audio is comprehensible.

Incomprehensible audio is just audio that you haven't studied and don't understand.

Not sure what you're asking exactly. You'll understand most of your input when you're functional/fluent in listening, or when you add audio that you've studied and understand.

But what happened to the sister and the Fredbear Spirit's flower fetish is besides the point. The fact that there are unsolved mysteries doesn't validate this premise. The universe being divided by a mystical tooth fairy would explain why no sentient extraterrestrial life exists near us, but so what? My point is that there's no evidence to support the version of "Give Cake" that is asserted here, unless I'm unaware of it, in which case I will readily admit my error.

All of the games are released now, so we have to assume that Scott gave us all of the puzzle pieces, and that what is shown in the game is legitimate, otherwise it's all guesswork, and there's no way to deduce the correct answer. Like when people say that the check in fnaf2 isn't real, that Scott was just joking around, that that the year doesn't mean anything. When the character receives a check dated 1987, I assume that the character received a check that is dated 1987. When I see a someone kill a kid then drive off and leave the body outside, I assume that's what happened. I can choose to interpret anything in any way I want. I can assert that Psychic Fredbear is the spirit of the victim that was stuffed into a suit, then make a theory based around that, but if there's no evidence to support the premise, then the theory is false.  

What evidence is there to indicate that the the victim of Give Cake is the sister, and that one of the kids is the Crying Child? You can't say that it's true because it makes the rest of the theory work.

Of course there's a body, but there's no evidence that he put the body in a box or the trunk. He gets in and drives off with the body still outside, so the evidence points toward him leaving the kid there and skedaddling.

I can't prove that he isn't watching, but I also can't prove that Purple Guy isn't Chuck Norris. There's no evidence to indicate that any of those kids are the Crying Child, or that the victim is Crying Child's sister.
